discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
motivation: Kane and Mele (2005) showed that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator, classified by a new Z2 invariant. Their work showed that insulators, long thought to be well understood, can differ in quantized, entanglement-related ways that no local order parameter captures. Molenkamp and his group confirmed this in 2007 by measuring quantized edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Together these results founded the field of topological insulators and, more broadly, symmetry-protected topological matter. That field now links band theory, quantum field theory anomalies, Majorana physics and materials discovery. It has changed how every condensed-matter physicist classifies phases of matter. It is a rare case where a deep, universal theoretical concept was quickly and unambiguously confirmed by experiment, and its conceptual influence has only grown in the two decades since.
